summary: Fenoverine is a smooth-muscle antispasmodic, structurally related to the phenothiazines, used for painful functional disorders of the gastrointestinal and biliary tract and dysmenorrhea. It is described as a calcium ion 'synchronizer' that normalizes smooth-muscle contraction. It is not FDA-approved and has been associated with reports of rhabdomyolysis, leading to restricted or withdrawn marketing in some countries; use with caution and avoid combination with statins.
indications: Symptomatic relief of spasm and pain in functional gastrointestinal disorders (e.g. irritable bowel syndrome)
Biliary and urinary tract spasm; primary dysmenorrhea (per local labeling)

moa: Fenoverine is a phenothiazine-related antispasmodic described as a calcium ion 'synchronizer': it modulates calcium fluxes across smooth-muscle cell membranes, restoring coordinated (synchronized) contraction and relieving both hypermotility (spasm) and hypomotility. This produces musculotropic antispasmodic effects on gastrointestinal, biliary and uterine smooth muscle without strong anticholinergic activity.

monitor: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness

preg: Safety in pregnancy is not established; avoid use during pregnancy unless considered essential by a physician.
lact: There are no data on excretion in human milk; avoid during breastfeeding.
renal: No specific renal dosing data; use with caution, particularly given the risk of rhabdomyolysis which can impair renal function.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; as a phenothiazine-related compound it undergoes hepatic metabolism.

major: Statins (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors) and other myotoxic drugs - additive risk of rhabdomyolysis; avoid combination
moderate: CNS depressants - possible additive sedation (phenothiazine relation)
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset; no specific food to avoid.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol due to possible additive central effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause elevated creatine kinase (CK) and myoglobinuria if rhabdomyolysis develops; monitor CK if muscle symptoms occur.

emergency: Rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury (severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine)

monitoring: Muscle symptoms - pain, tenderness, weakness; check creatine kinase if suspected
Renal function if rhabdomyolysis is suspected
counsel: Take with food; use only as long as needed for cramps/spasm
Stop the medicine and seek urgent care if you get unexplained muscle pain, weakness or dark-colored urine
Do not take with cholesterol-lowering statins unless your doctor knows
Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine

pearls: Not FDA-approved; record based on EMA/national product information and pharmacovigilance reports, pending clinical review. Marketed in parts of Europe and Asia.
Associated with rhabdomyolysis - a key reason for regulatory restriction in several countries; AVOID combining with statins
Described as a calcium 'synchronizer' rather than a simple smooth-muscle relaxant
Phenothiazine-related structure but used as a GI/biliary antispasmodic, not as an antipsychotic
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless the next dose is near, then skip it. Do not double up. Resume the usual schedule.
overdose: Overdose data are limited; expect exaggerated GI and CNS effects and a potential for muscle toxicity. Management is symptomatic and supportive; monitor for rhabdomyolysis (CK, renal function) and treat accordingly.
